gen_risks.description: School mentoring funding disbursed directly to primary school clusters may not be properly monitored, risking misallocation or improper reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and adopt simplified guidelines for school mentoring funding within the Project Operations Manual and conduct internal audit oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: There is a risk that school mentoring funding, which is to be spent at the schools, may not be properly monitored.

gen_risks.description: Workload overload among FM staff at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance could delay transaction processing and financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint adequate financial management staff, including government officers and consultants, within three months of project signing.
gen_risks.evidence: The current FM staff at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance may be overloaded, potentially leading to delays in processing transactions and reporting.

gen_risks.description: Delays in approving the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) could impede the timely execution of planned project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt a simplified AWPB template and standardized approval timeline in the Financial Management Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: The delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) may hinder the timely implementation of project activities.

gen_risks.description: Limited staff knowledge and experience with World Bank Procurement Regulations could result in procurement noncompliance and schedule slippage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign full-time procurement officers to the project and deliver targeted procurement and contract management training.
gen_risks.evidence: MoEYS staff’s limited knowledge and experience with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations, potentially resulting in project implementation delays and noncompliance

gen_risks.description: Delays in receiving technical inputs and obtaining internal clearance from the procurement review committee may disrupt procurement processing timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish explicit service standards in the POM, track procurement inputs via STEP, and delegate review authority to committee members.
gen_risks.evidence: possible delays in receiving technical inputs for procurement; ... possible delays in internal clearance from procurement review committee.

gen_risks.description: Governance and corruption risks during procurement transactions could undermine project resource allocation and fairness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce enhanced disclosure of procurement information, publish contract awards quarterly, and implement a robust complaint handling mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: governance risks, including corrupt practices in procurement;

gen_risks.description: Inadequate capacity for contract supervision and management may lead to poor vendor performance and delivery delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted contract management training to the procurement team and designate technical department focal points for cross-departmental coordination.
gen_risks.evidence: inadequate capacity for contract supervision and management, which may result in implementation delays

gen_risks.description: Climate change hazards such as severe flooding, tropical cyclones, and extreme heat threaten school infrastructure damage and educational continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct classrooms and childcare centers using climate-resilient, elevated designs, solar panels, and expand e-learning platforms for emergency instruction.
gen_risks.evidence: Natural disasters caused by climate change, including floods, cyclones, and extreme heat, pose significant challenges for Cambodia, particularly affecting the continuity of education.

gen_risks.description: Scaling up Early Grade Learning (EGL) and targeted instruction nationally through government systems may encounter capability constraints that reduce program fidelity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an implementation science-informed learning agenda utilizing rapid testing, process evaluations, and adaptive adjustments.
gen_risks.evidence: Transitioning from successful, donor-funded interventions with limited geographic coverage to implementation at scale through government systems requires overcoming the many technical, financial, political economy, and capability constraints

gen_risks.description: The Early Learning Partnership Trust Fund closing date in April 2027 precedes the project closing date in 2030, risking premature interruption of childcare grant funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Front-load trust fund disbursements for Subcomponent 1.1 and integrate childcare training into the National Preschool Teacher Training Center prior to 2027.
gen_risks.evidence: The closing date for the Trust Fund differs from that of the project. The Trust Fund is scheduled to close on April 30, 2027.

gen_risks.description: The phase-out of key development partner assistance by 2027 may cause monitoring and evaluation gaps and financial sustainability challenges for EGL programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Build ministry M&E capacity, digitize progress tracking, and institutionalize cluster-based mentoring funding within regular government operations.
gen_risks.evidence: Their support is expected to phase out by 2027. Due to these one-off interventions, there are gaps in M&E for building the ministry’s capacity to sustain programs.

gen_risks.description: HRMIS modernization progression to Phase 2 depends on Phase 1 proving technical quality and regulatory feasibility; delays or failure in Phase 1 could stall rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a formal joint working group with the Ministry of Civil Service to align system scoping and functional mapping during Phase 1.
gen_risks.evidence: Progression to Phase 2 is conditional on Phase 1 results demonstrating quality and feasibility in terms of technical and system development

gen_risks.description: Small, dispersed procurement packages for community school buildings may fail to attract competitive bidders or lead to inconsistent construction quality across subnational areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize structured open national and subnational procurement approaches, group adjacent works where viable, and enforce standardized supervision guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: These packages would not be attractive to the international market and will therefore be procured through open national and subnational approaches

gen_risks.description: Civil works for classroom, preschool, and childcare construction pose potential environmental and social risks (e.g., land acquisition, impacts on indigenous peoples).
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply the Environmental and Social Management Framework, conduct land and indigenous peoples screening, and implement universal accessibility design standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social Risk Classification: Substantial

gen_risks.description: Prevalence of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and risk of SEA/SH during infrastructure expansion and school activities could harm vulnerable students and community members.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver teacher training on GBV awareness, implement a GBV prevention action plan, and operationalize a dedicated SEA/SH grievance redress mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Tackling GBV remains a paramount concern in Cambodia... significant lack of comprehensive data on GBV prevalence, overall, in the education sector

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk is rated Substantial due to (a) limited institutional capacity to manage environmental and social risks and impacts; (b) nationwide implementation of the project's activities; (c) possible exclusion of vulnerable groups (such as poor children, children with disabilities, and indigenous groups); and (d) other risks involving child protection, occupational health and safety, labor issues, and sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH).
gt_risks.mitigation: The project will develop a capacity-building plan for the Environmental and Social Safeguards Office and Project Management Unit, including hiring dedicated environmental and social specialists and providing targeted training. It will establish robust monitoring mechanisms to ensure support for vulnerable groups (universal design in new school/WASH construction, materials adapted for visually impaired students), strict adherence to worker codes of conduct, complaint redress and referral mechanisms, and construction site safety measures to protect school children and communities from labor influx and construction-related risks.
